Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132" 0 Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 796, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Windham and Gorham the Little Falls Veterans
Memorial Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 796.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 2787.
Thank you.

Testimony of Senator Tim Nangle introducing
LD 796, "Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Windham and Gorham the Little Falls
Veterans Memorial Bridge"
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
March 25, 2025
Representative Crafts, and distinguished colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation, as you know, my name is Tim Nangle. I represent Senate District 26, which includes
the communities of Windham, Raymond, Casco, Frye Island, and part of Westbrook.
I'm pleased to bring forward LD 796, a resolve to rename MDOT Bridge #2787 on Route 202 --~
currently known as the South Windham Bridge ---- as the Little Falls Veterans Memorial Bridge. This bridge spans the Presumpscot River between the towns of Windham and Gorham, in a part of the community historically known as Little Falls.
Attached to my testimony is a letter from the Windham Town Council expressing their unanimous
support for this renaming. The Council also communicated with town management in Gorham and confirmed they do not foresee any issues with the adjoining bridge being renamed.
Windham has a strong and active veterans community, anchored by organizations like Field-Allen
American Legion Post 148 and VFW Post 10643 which jointly operate the Windham Veterans Center.
These organizations not only honor the service of local veterans but also serve as vital community hubs for support, connection, and remembrance.
As you know, these types of memorial namings are common and meaningful ways to recognize local service and sacrifice. I hope you'll join me in supporting this community-driven request.
I'm happy to answer any questions.
